routes.label: Read the base and height from coordinates

question:
The area in square units of the region enclosed by parallelogram \(ABCD\) is

[Figure 1](figures/1991_AMC_8_Q10_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
A parallelogram's area is its base times the perpendicular height. Here \(AD\) lies on the \(x\)-axis, so its opposite side \(BC\) is parallel to that axis.

Since \(C=(4,2)\), every point on \(BC\) has height \(2\). Point \(B\) lies on the \(y\)-axis, so \(B=(0,2)\). Therefore the horizontal base has length
\[
BC=4-0=4.
\]
The perpendicular distance from \(BC\) to \(AD\), which lies at height \(0\), is \(2\). Hence
\[
\text{Area}=4\cdot2=\boxed{8}
\]
square units, choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
